title: Spending wisely (budgeting)

screens.title: Lesson 8: Spending wisely
screens.text: Spending wisely means making a plan before we spend. Let us make one. Press Start when you are ready.

art.alt: A plan and a thinking face

screens.text: A week of schoolwork and chores earns about 50 tokens, which is about 10 dollars. A plan says where the tokens will go before we spend them.

art.alt: About 50 tokens a week, and a plan

screens.text: Here is one example plan for 50 tokens: 30 saved for the treasure, and 20 for special treats. That is 2 special treats at 10 tokens each. It adds up to 50.
Now a store story. At a store, a balance is 20 dollars. Someone swipes 4 dollars for a snack. Now the balance is 16 dollars.

art.alt: Swipe 4 dollars: the balance goes from 20 dollars to 16 dollars

screens.text: Next they swipe 6 dollars for a pencil case for school. Now the balance is 10 dollars. Each swipe makes the balance smaller, so we check the balance before every swipe.

art.alt: Swipe 6 dollars: the balance goes from 16 dollars to 10 dollars

screens.prompt: The balance is 10 dollars. At the store, a book is 5 dollars and another pencil case is 6 dollars. Can both be bought?

options.label: No. 5 plus 6 is more than 10. Pick one that fits.
options.why: Yes, that is the careful answer. 5 plus 6 is 11, and there is only 10. Choose one.

options.label: Yes, swipes are free.
options.why: A swipe is not free. It takes real money, and only 10 dollars is left.

options.label: Yes, just swipe and see.
options.why: Checking first is wiser than swiping and hoping. Check the balance before a swipe.

screens.prompt: Which is the wiser purchase this week?

options.label: Another treat, right after one.
options.why: That is a want, and it takes tokens away from the treasure.

options.label: Something we need for school.
options.why: Needs come first. A thing we need is a wiser purchase than another want.

options.label: Whatever is shiniest in the shop.
options.why: Shiny things are tempting. A plan helps us pick on purpose.

screens.text: If a plan runs out before the week ends, that is a good thing to talk about. It teaches us to keep some tokens for later and to plan smaller next time.

screens.prompt: Our plan has 20 tokens for treats. On Tuesday we use all 20. It is only Tuesday. What is the best next step?

options.label: Take the tokens from the treasure.
options.why: Then the treasure moves later. It is better to wait for next week.

options.label: Spend tokens we have not earned yet.
options.why: We can only spend tokens we have. Next week brings more.

options.label: Wait for next week’s tokens, and plan fewer treats next time.
options.why: Yes. We stick to the plan and learn from it. The treasure tokens stay safe.

talk.q: Look at one real store receipt together. What was bought, and how much was it?
talk.note: The balance goes down with every swipe. Check it before swiping. Store prices are in dollars, not family tokens.

talk.q: How would we like to plan the 50 tokens a week?
talk.note: The plan in the lesson (30 for the treasure, 20 for treats) is only an example. Change it to fit your family.

talk.q: What do we do when the treat tokens run out early?
talk.note: Wait for next week, and plan smaller next time. It is not a failure.

talk.q: If a child pressed Ask a grown-up in this lesson, what was the question?
talk.note: Common ones: a plan that runs out before the week ends (a good talk point) and "what if I want more treats?" (talk about the trade-off with the treasure).
